newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Congo peace talks edge closer to accord.
newsitem.headline: Congo peace talks edge closer to accord.

text.p: Congolese President Pascal Lissouba and rival Denis Sassou Nguesso are edging closer to a solution to a conflict that has killed hundreds of people in Brazzaville since June, diplomats said on Wednesday.
The main stumbling block remained the selection of a neutral interim prime minister to oversee the transition to presidential elections.

"We need to resolve one last-ditch problem -- it largely concerns the criteria for the selection of the head of the government," Mohamed Sahnoun, the special envoy for the United Nations and Organisation for African Unity, told Reuters by phone from Libreville, the capital of Gabon.
Gabonese president Omar Bongo has been leading the mediation effort with Sahnoun.

Sahnoun said Bongo was sending a high-powered delegation to Brazzaville to meet all the parties in the conflict, and some delegates to the Libreville talks may be also be returning home to liaise with their allies.
They would return to Libreville in coming days, mediators said.

The conflict blew up in June when forces loyal to Lissouba surrounded the villa of ex-president Sassou in Brazzaville in a crackdown on militias ahead of presidential elections that had been scheduled for July 27.
The election was postponed. Both Sassou and Lissouba are likely to be candidates when it is finally held.
